function: MIMO detection: learned fixed-point quantization (per-variable fractional bitwidths) of the MMSE-WeJi massive MIMO detector, cutting bitwidth and complexity while preserving BER (p. 1).
system: Nt x Nr = 8 x 128 and 16 x 128 MIMO, 64-QAM, real-valued equivalent model; no RIS; frequency band not stated (p. 2, p. 3).
method: DL-AQUA: learnable quantization step sizes trained by back-propagation through the detector, with straight-through estimator, Gumbel-Softmax SER-approximating loss, adaptive bitwidth penalty; supervised, Adam (p. 2-4).
data_channel: Simulated i.i.d. Rayleigh fading with AWGN, channel known at receiver; training (10^4 samples) and testing samples generated randomly and independently (p. 2, p. 4).
test_conditions: Trained at the maximum test SNR; tested over 2-12 dB (8x128) and 5-15 dB (16x128); separate bitwidth assignment per antenna configuration (p. 4).
baselines: Classical: full-precision FP32 MMSE-WeJi and unified quantization (UQ); learned: AHPQ [6], deep-reinforcement-learning hybrid-precision quantization; plus randomly generated bitwidth assignments (p. 1, p. 4).
metrics: BER versus SNR, SNR loss at BER 10^-3, average bitwidth, BER-bitwidth trade-off, normalized complexity in bit operations (BOPs), approximate SER loss during adaptive penalty search (p. 4-5).
complexity: Normalized bit-operation (BOPs) count of the quantized detector, Table II: 49.50% and 55.01% of UQ versus 66.43% and 66.41% for AHPQ; training cost not reported (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "the channel matrix is assumed to be independently identically distributed (i.i.d.) Rayleigh fading channel matrix" - a custom i.i.d. Rayleigh simulation; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 4: "The SNR for training is set to the maximum of the testing SNR." - only an SNR sweep; each antenna configuration gets its own trained bitwidth assignment (Fig. 2, p. 4), so nothing is tested in an untrained configuration.
q3_support: p. 4: "we compare the BER performance of MMSE-WeJi quantized by three schemes: UQ, AHPQ [6], and DL-AQUA" - UQ is the non-learned empirical quantization; AHPQ is an earlier deep-reinforcement-learning quantizer for MIMO detectors (p. 1).
q4_support: p. 5: "The normalized complexity of AHPQ and DL-AQUA relative to UQ is given in Table II" - bit-operation (BOPs) counts; DL-AQUA needs 49.50% and 55.01% of the UQ complexity.
q5_support: p. 4: "Samples for training and testing are generated randomly and independently." - synthetic samples only; no code or data link and no public channel dataset.
notes: Eligibility is borderline: the learned element is the per-variable fixed-point quantization of a classical MMSE-WeJi detector, trained end to end through the detector with an SER loss (p. 2-3), read like deep unfolding with trained parameters; area 1 by its BER metric. Reviewer to confirm. q4 rests on normalized, not absolute, BOPs counts (Table II, p. 5). Integral bitwidths come from a non-learned PDF clipping rule (p. 3).
